# Benchpress

> The reliability layer for AI agents with write access. A task-agnostic control loop (policy sweep → resolve and lock look-alikes → definition of done → plan → gate every write in code → read every write back → verify → deliver a receipt) that wraps any tool layer. Published on PyPI as `benchpress-agent` (Apache-2.0, Python 3.12+). Built for the Multi-App AI Agent Hackathon, 2026-09-13.

Try it with no keys: `uvx --from benchpress-agent benchpress demo`. It runs the real loop, gate and read-back on an in-memory workspace with a scripted model, and shows the gate refusing a planted write to a look-alike record.

## Start here
- [README](https://github.com/rajkaria/benchpress/blob/main/README.md): product story, architecture, the eight phases, the gate, substrates, results, disclosure
- [PyPI page](https://pypi.org/project/benchpress-agent/): install and API quickstart (source: docs/PYPI.md)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/rajkaria/benchpress/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): every release shipped during the hackathon, 0.1.0 onward
- [Reliability brief](https://github.com/rajkaria/benchpress/blob/main/docs/RELIABILITY-BRIEF.md): numbers, methods, failures, cost
- [VISION](https://github.com/rajkaria/benchpress/blob/main/VISION.md): what it becomes, business model

## Public API (Python)
- `benchpress.wrap(model, executor, providers=[...], policy_packs=...)` → `Benchpress`; `await agent.run(request, trace_dir=...)` → `TrialResult` (`status` is computed from read-back evidence; `context.refusals` lists every refused write with its rule)
- `benchpress.run_trial(...)`: the loop itself; `benchpress.Gate`, `benchpress.ModelConfig`, `benchpress.Ablations`
- `benchpress.load_policy_packs([...])`, `benchpress.available_policy_packs()`: code-enforced rule sets
- `benchpress.rehearse.rehearse(...)` / `replay(...)`: run N times on fresh stages, require convergence, replay the plan with no model
- `benchpress.shims.mcp.mcp_executor(...)` (extra `[mcp]`), `benchpress.shims.openai_agents.guard_tools(...)` (extra `[openai-agents]`)

## CLI
- `benchpress demo`: offline end-to-end demo with receipts
- `benchpress run --providers slack,gmail,hubspot,stripe --prompt ... [--policy-pack billing]`: real apps
- `benchpress receipt DIR --html`: receipt summary and self-contained page
- `benchpress gate check [PATH]`: the public gate-rule corpus (152 cases, all passing)
- `benchpress policy list|show NAME`
- `benchpress rehearse ... --n 3` / `benchpress replay rehearsal.json`
- `benchpress mcp-guard --policy guard.json -- <upstream MCP server>`

## Evidence (claim discipline: we never say "passed ArgaBench")
- [reports/summary.md](https://github.com/rajkaria/benchpress/blob/main/reports/summary.md): every scored trial. Benchmark: ArgaBench ECOM-02 (0/111 across 37 frontier configurations in Arga's published data).
  - Local twins of the published seed under ArgaBench's **unmodified runner and grader**: Benchpress 3/3 pass, same-model baseline 0/3.
  - Real Slack/Gmail/HubSpot/Stripe (test mode), scored by a line-cited port of ArgaBench's criteria: Benchpress 0/2 and baseline 0/2. Both arms fail; Benchpress fails one assertion (A2), the baseline fails three (A2, A5, A6). Neither real-app arm was unsafe.
- [reports/INDEX.md](https://github.com/rajkaria/benchpress/blob/main/reports/INDEX.md): how to verify any number
- [reports/gate-replay-historical.md](https://github.com/rajkaria/benchpress/blob/main/reports/gate-replay-historical.md): the gate replayed against ArgaBench's own recorded trials
- No claim about the official ArgaBench leaderboard. The substrate, prep work, failures and cost are all disclosed in the README.

## Engineering
- Task-agnostic by construction: CI greps the agent package for benchmark task ids and seeded entities
- pyright strict, ruff, 880+ tests; CI also builds the wheel, installs it into a clean venv on Python 3.12 and 3.13, and runs `demo`, `gate check` and `policy list`
